headline: Finance committee to review ELL curriculum purchase, special education contracts, and FY27 financial reports.
summary: The committee will discuss a $33,000 ELL digital license purchase, several special education contracts and renewals for FY27, and review the FY27 July transfer and financial reports.
items: ELL Curriculum Purchase: recommendation to approve 330 digital licenses for HMH's English 3D program, plus teacher licenses and two teacher guides, not to exceed $33,000.00

Special Education Contracts, Addendums, and Renewals: ESS addendum for one Mental Health Technician at Birch Hill Elementary, not to exceed $98,000.00; Rockingham Contracting and Therapy Services renewal for 1.6 SLP positions, not to exceed $211,680.00; Stepping Stones Group renewal for 1.0 SLP and 1.0 ASL Interpreter, not to exceed $236,880.00; SLP for Mama-to-be renewal for part-time SLP leave coverage, not to exceed $46,900.00; Carroll Center renewal for Orientation and Mobility services, not to exceed $135,990.00; Clark Associates updated contract correction for Occupational Therapy Services, not to exceed $1,061,483.00; grant-funded contracts for audiology, AAC services, nursing, and charter school special education services (FYI only)

MEMORANDUM 
 
TO:  Finance & Operations Committee 
 
FROM:  ELL Department 
 
DATE:  August 24, 2026 
 
SUBJ:  Request for MNH English 3D Digital Licenses 
 
The ELL Department is recommending the purchase 330 digital licenses for HMH’s English 
3D program, along with teacher digital licenses and two teacher guides in the amount of 
$33,000. These licenses will be used in English language learner classes at both Nashua 
High School North and Nashua High School South. All student and teacher licenses will be 
valid for two years. 
The Nashua School District’s ELL program has used HMH’s English 3D curriculum since 
2023 (BOE approved). Renewing the digital licenses will allow students to continue 
accessing the curriculum and instructional resources currently in use and will provide 
consistency and continuity in their educational experience. 
Beginning in the 2027–2028 school year, the ELL Department will initiate a comprehensive 
curriculum evaluation process. ELL administrators and teachers will review curricula from 
multiple publishers and evaluate their effectiveness in meeting the needs of Nashua’s 
English language learners. Based on this evaluation, the department will determine 
whether to continue using English 3D or recommend a different curriculum for future 
adoption.  This two-year license will give continuity of instruction while we review future 
curriculum. 
 
Recommendation to approve the purchase of 330 digital licenses for HMH’s English 3D 
program, along with teacher digital license and two teacher guides for use in the high 
school ELL classes during the 2026-27 and 2027-2028 school years in an amount not to 
exceed $33,000.00.
MEMORANDUM 
 
To:      Nashua Board of Education 
 
From: Special Education Department 
 
Date:  August 17, 2026 
 
RE:      Special Education Contracts, Addendums and Renewals for FY 27 
 
 
Program Staffing (MA, FV, AF, KD): 
 
● Effective School Solutions (ESS) - ADDENDUM. This contract addendum builds upon 
the existing partnership with ESS to add one Mental Health Technician (MHT) to serve 
at Birch Hill Elementary at a cost not to exceed $98,000.00 above the original contract 
for the 2026-27 school year.  The partnership with ESS and the staffing of this MHT 
position serves a unique need in augmenting the District’s elementary Project 
Achievement programs with a high level of mental health supports and trauma-informed 
practice.  Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.  
 
Recommendation to approve the contract addendum with ESS for staffing one additional 
full-time MHT for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $98,000.00.  Funding 
to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services. 
 
 
 
Related Services Staffing and Services: 
 
● Rockingham Contracting and Therapy Services, LLC - RENEWAL.  Staffing for 1.6 
full-time Speech and Language Pathologists at $105/hr, for a cost not to exceed 
$211,680.00 for the 2026-27 school year.  Funding to be charged to the Operating 
Budget under Contracted Services.  
 
Recommendation to approve the contract with Rockingham for staffing of 1.6 SLP 
positions for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $211,680.00.  Funding to 
be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services. 
 
 
 
● Stepping Stones Group (SSG) - RENEWAL.  Staffing for 1.0 full-time Speech and 
Language Pathologist at $94/hr and 1.0 full-time ASL Interpreter at $94/hr, for a total 
cost not to exceed $236,880.00 for the 2026-27 school year.  Funding to be charged to 
the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.  
 
Recommendation to approve the contract with SSG for staffing of 1.0 SLP position and 
1.0 ASL Interpreter position for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed 
$236,880.00.  Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.
● SLP for Mama-to-be, LLC - RENEWAL.  Staffing for part-time Speech Language 
Pathologist (SLP) services for the purpose of covering planned leaves of Nashua SLP 
providers during the 26-27 school year, at a cost of $134/hour, not to exceed $46,900.00 
for the school year.  Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted 
Services.  
 
Recommendation to approve the contract with SLP for Mama-to-be for staffing of part-
time SLP leave-coverage for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed 
$46,900.00.  Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services. 
 
 
 
● Carroll Center - RENEWAL.  Orientation & Mobility services for a cost not to exceed 
$135,990.00 for the 2026-27 school year.  Funding to be charged to IDEA Grant (IEP 
students) and Operating Budget (504 students) under Contracted Services.  
 
Recommendation to approve the contract with Carroll Center for Orientation and Mobility 
services for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $135,990.00.  Funding to 
be charged to the IDEA Grant for IEP students and the Operating Budget (Contracted 
Services) for students under 504 plan.

● Alternative Augmentative Communication (AAC) services from Boothby Therapy 
Services to be funded from the IDEA Grant.  Estimated cost: $40,000.

MEMORANDUM 
 
TO:  F&O Committee/BOE 
FROM:   Krystal De Gray, COO 
DATE:  8/17/26 
SUBJ:  Clark Associates Correction  
 
During the July 20, 2026 Board of Education meeting, the contract and addendum with 
Clark Associates for Occupational Therapy Services was approved with the following 
motion: 
Recommendation to approve the contract with Clark Associates for the 2026-27 school year 
at a cost not to exceed $976,522.50.  Funding to be charged to account 91.1.022160 53614. 
It has come to our attention that only the weekly services were included and the following 
annual services were omitted 1) the extended school year services ($22,950), 2) cost of 
evaluations ($36,000), and 3) IEP updates ($26,010).   Attached please find the update 
contract and addendum that includes services for both school year and the extended school 
year for 2026-27. 
Recommendation to approve the updated contract with Clark Associates for the 
2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $1,061,483.00.  Funding to be charged to 
account 91.1.022160 53614.
Contract for Services 
Nashua School District 
 
 
 
This Contract for Services is between Clark Associates, 5 Happy Lane, Londonderry, NH  03053 (the 
“Contractor”) and Nashua School District, 141 Ledge St., Nashua, NH 03060 (the “District”) for services 
to be provided.  
 
The contract is governed by the following documents, in order of priority: 
1.  This contract for services.  
2.  Purchase Order No.:  
3.  2026-27 Addendum A, Independent Agreement for Occupational Therapy   
Any discrepancy or contradiction in the above documents shall be determined by their order of priority. 
 
Objective of Services:    
To provide Occupational Therapy Services for the 2026-2027 School Year 
 
Description of Services:    
The Contractor will provide Occupational Therapy Services to Special Education identified students 
across the district under the student’s Individual Education Plan.  These services will include direct 
services, indirect services, consultation, instruction, documentations, meetings, evaluations, and extended 
school year using properly qualified and certified personnel. 
 
Service Venue:  
District Wide, on-site at School Facilities.  Contract therapists may, at times, need to Zoom from a 
location outside of the school buildings (e.g., their car, home office, etc.) in order to attend meetings that 
occur outside of their scheduled hours in the District. 
 
Compensation and Payment 
The District agrees to pay Contractor up to the sum not to exceed $1,061,483.00 for the above-described 
services.  
The District will make payment to the Contractor at its next regular payment date for completed services 
upon receipt of an approved invoice with required documentation.  An IRS Form W-9 must be on file 
with the District. 
 
Contract Period: 
July 1, 2026 thru June 30, 2027 
 
Rights:  
Subject to the terms of this Agreement, all reports, studies and other work product utilizing or containing 
information or data from the District shall be the sole and exclusive property of the District.  The 
Contractor agrees to keep confidential all such District information and data.    
 
Termination:  
This Agreement may be terminated upon thirty (30) days written notice by either party to this Agreement.  
Such termination shall not be deemed to be a breach of this Agreement, nor shall it be deemed to be 
tortious conduct. Upon termination, Contractor will present the District with a final invoice reflecting: a) 
any unbilled consulting fees due through the most recently completed project phase; and b) costs incurred
since the completion of the most recently completed phase. The District agrees to pay this final invoice 
within 30 days of receipt.  
Termination for Cause:   
This agreement may be terminated by the District on seven (7) calendar days’ written notice to the 
Contractor in the event of a failure by the Contractor to adhere to all the terms and conditions of the 
contract or failure to satisfactorily, in the sole opinion of the District, provide contracted services in a 
timely and professional manner.  The Contractor shall be given an opportunity for consultation with the 
District prior to the effective date of the termination. 
 
Subcontracting:   
No assignment, transfer, delegation or subcontracting will be allowed under this contract for services 
without the expressed prior written consent of the District. 
 
Independent Contractor Status:   
The parties agree that the Contractor shall have the status of and shall perform all work under this contract 
as an independent contractor, maintaining control over all its subcontractors and employees.  The only 
contractual relationship created by this contract is between the District and Contractor, and nothing in this 
contract shall create any contractual relationship between the District and Contractor’s subcontractors or 
employees.  The parties also agree that the Contractor is not a District employee and will receive no 
benefits as such. 
 
Governing Law:   
This Agreement is to be governed and construed under the laws of the State of New Hampshire, and any 
action to enforce this contract must be brought forward in a State of New Hampshire court of competent 
jurisdiction. 
 
Entire Agreement: 
This Contract for Services is the entire agreement between the parties regarding the services, and the 
agreement may not be modified except by a written agreement signed by both parties. 
 
The foregoing is agreed to by the undersigned authorized representatives of the parties: 
 
 
 
           
For       Date 
 
 
           
For       Nashua School District   Date
Addendum A  
 
Independent Agreement for Occupational Therapy Services 
  
 
Section 1 
 
Clark Associates, including its subcontractors and employees (“Independent Contractor”), and the 
Nashua School District (“Purchaser”) agree that occupational therapy services (“O.T.”) for the 202 6-2027 
school year shall be provided to students of said District by Independent Contractor and that Purchaser 
shall pay for said services pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.  
 
The Independent Contractor guarantees that students receiving its services pursuant to this Agreement 
shall be provided all of the rights and protections afforded under the IDEA, ADA and in accordance with 
all other relevant federal, state and local statutes and administrative rules and regulations.  
 
The Independent Contractor will make available to the Purchaser and cooperate in the review and audit 
of all records relating to this Agreement and in accordance with 34 CR 74.20:34 CFR 74.24 (c) and 34 
CFR 74.166.  This also includes contracts and agreements between Independent Contractor and any 
individuals, companies or other entities providing services or materials that relate to this Agreement.  
 
Section II 
 
1. FEES. The sum of $1,061,483.00 is the maximum authorized funding level for occupational 
therapy services for the 2026-2027 school year.  Independent Contractor shall bill services as 
follows: $76.50/hr. ($38.25 per half hour unit) for direct service, indirect services, consultation, 
instruction, documentation, and meetings as required; $300.00 per evaluation. A mileage fee for 
out-of- district travel may be charged at the IRS mileage rate in effect at the time the mileage is 
incurred. No fees will be charged for-in-district travel time or mileage.  The Independent 
Contractor will provide necessary consultation to para-educators during student therapy units. 
 
The total projected cost for occupational therapy services submitted by Clark Associates for the 
2026-2027 school year is $1,061,483.00.  The sum of $1,061,483.00 is the current maximum 
authorized funding level by the Nashua School district for occupational therapy services for the 
2026-2027 school year.  
 
The Independent Contractor shall provide occupational therapy services, including direct 
services, indirect services, consultation, instruction, documentations, meetings, evaluations, and 
extended school year using properly qualified and certified personnel from July 1, 2026, through 
June 30, 2027. 
   
Should the Independent Contractor conclude during the term of this Agreement that the 
occupational therapy services will consume the budgeted amount and extend beyond the 
allocated sum of $1,061,483.00 the contractor shall notify Purchaser’s Director of Special 
Education, in writing at least 90 days prior to the anticipated exhaustion of those budgeted funds.  
The provision of services beyond the allocated sum by the Purchaser must be approved in writing 
by the Director of Special Education.  Furthermore, the Independent Contractor shall generate 
quarterly school year expenditure reports for the benefit of the Purchaser. 
 
The Purchaser specifically reserves the right to contract with other agencies or individuals for 
O.T. services during the 2026-2027 school year should the authorized funding level 
($1,061,483.00) be exceeded during the 2026-2027 school year (including services provided 
during the Summer of 2026).
The Independent Contractor shall not deliver services to students who are not identified as 
educationally disabled or students with educational disabilities who do not have services in their 
Individual Education Plan, unless specifically approved by the Director of Special Education.  
 
The Director of Special education will authorize screening referrals for non-identified students. 
 
2. SPACE, EQUIPMENT & SUPPLIES shall be provided by the Purchaser after consultation with 
Independent Contractor.  Independent Contractor shall not purchase supplies and equipment 
without prior authorization by Purchaser (Director of Special Education).  The Independent 
Contractor will maintain a list of district supplies and equipment to be reviewed by the Purchaser 
on a regular basis at no administrative cost to the district.  The Purchaser (Special Education 
Department) will maintain a list of its occupational therapy supplies and equipment.  Independent 
Contractor shall, on a regular basis, review the said supply and equipment list. Independent 
Contractor shall provide to Purchaser (Director of Special Education), at no cost to Purchaser, an 
accounting of all supplies and equipment related to the provision of occupational therapy services 
(including the location of said supplies and equipment) during October 2026. 
 
3. Independent Contractor, including any and all of its independent contractors or subcontractors, 
will provide written records, documentation, and supervision as requested by the Purchaser and 
in accordance with A.O.T.A. professional standards.   
 
4. Independent Contractor (and its personnel and subcontractors) shall obtain and maintain all 
necessary professional certifications and licenses. The Independent Contractor, each employee 
or subcontractor of the Independent Contractor shall provide to the Purchaser certificate(s) of 
professional liability insurance naming the City of Nashua as an additional insured. Said 
certificate(s) shall be in the amount(s) required by the Purchaser and delivered to Purchaser 
within two weeks of the signing of this contract.   
 
5. Independent Contractor and all its personnel shall maintain current occupational therapy clinical 
notes in accordance with A.O.T.A. professional standards that record the nature and procedures 
used in the provision of all occupational therapy units and will provide consultation, as needed, to 
para-educators for the purpose of Medicaid Billing.  Clinical notes shall be made available to 
Purchaser upon request by Purchaser. 
 
6. SCHEDULING of occupational therapy services, subject to the approval of Purchaser’s Director 
of Special Education, will be based on the availability of therapist(s) and every effort will be made 
to accommodate student/teacher schedules and new students with occupational therapy needs.  
All individual occupational therapist’s schedules will be provided to Purchaser (Director of Special 
Education) no later than September 30, 2026. Any deviation from these schedules, including 
absences, or changes in personnel, must be reported immediately to Purchaser’s Special 
Education Office. 
 
7. BILLING shall be submitted on a bi-weekly basis. Payments to the Independent Contractor for 
services provided and properly invoiced shall be made by the Purchaser within thirty (30) days of 
receipt of each itemized invoice. 
 
At the end of the school year, all outstanding invoices must be submitted within fifteen (15) days 
of the last date of service to ensure payment is processed within the applicable cont ract fiscal 
year. The final invoice for the school year must be clearly marked "FINAL INVOICE”. 
 
8. CONTRACT PERIOD for this Agreement is from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027. Any 
occupational therapy services to be delivered during the summer of 2026 pursuant to an 
extension of this Agreement shall be negotiated during March 2026.
9. Any personnel related concerns shall be addressed directly with the Independent Contractor (Deb 
Clark) by Purchaser’s Director of Special Education.  The Purchaser has the right to refuse the 
services of an individual subcontractor or employee under this contract, should the Purchaser 
deem the subcontractor to be unsuitable, for any reason, to provide occupational therapy 
services.  The Purchaser agrees to consult with the Independent Contractor (Deb Clark) prior to 
making such a determination. 
  
10. This contract may be terminated immediately by either party for failure of the other party to abide 
by the terms of the contract. However, either party will first be given an opportu nity to cure a 
default within ten (10) days of receipt of written notice of default, unless the default involves a 
failure to deliver occupational therapy services in a manner which subjects the Purchaser to 
violations of state and federal laws. 
 
11.  The Independent Contractor agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Purchaser from 
and against any and all damage, loss, injury, cost or expense (including attorney’s fees related to 
defending claims and to enforcing this indemnity provision) suffered or incurred by the Purchaser 
as a consequence of services provided by the Independent Contractor, which are not due to the 
negligence or intentional acts of the Purchaser, its agents or employees. 
 
12. The Purchaser agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Independent Contractor from 
and against any and all damage, loss, injury, cost or expense (including attorney’s fees related to   
defending claims and to enforcing this indemnity provision) suffered or incurred by the 
Independent Contractor as a consequence of utilizing the facilities and equipment of the 
Purchaser, which are not due to the negligence or intentional acts of the Independent Contractor, 
its agents or employees. 
13. Should Clark Associates be unable to acquire the necessary number of staff to s ervice children 
as required by those children’s I.E.P.s, the Nashua School District will take all necessary steps to 
deliver the services and units required by the children’s I.E.P.s by contracting with providers other 
than Clark Associates. 
 
Funding for these other providers will reduce the available annual funding set forth in  
Section II, 1.
